chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who died as a Saroura (one who has not yet performed Hajj) and had not performed the Hajj of Islam, and he had wealth, he (peace be upon him) said: A Saroura (one who has not yet performed Hajj) would perform Hajj on his behalf, the one who does not have any wealth.

key_terms.حَجَّةَ الْإِسْلَامِ: The first obligatory Hajj performed by a Muslim
key_terms.صَرُورَةٍ: A person who has not yet performed their obligatory Hajj
key_terms.لَا مَالَ لَهُ: One who does not have wealth (referring to the performer of Hajj for the deceased)

ai.seo_question: Who performs Hajj for a deceased person who died without performing their obligatory Hajj?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi clarifies that a 'Saroura'—one who has not yet fulfilled their own obligatory Hajj—may perform Hajj on behalf of a deceased person who died without having done so, provided the deceased left sufficient wealth. This highlights the Shia juristic view that the obligation of Hajj can be transferred to the estate, allowing the proxy to use the deceased's funds even before settling their own primary duty, emphasizing the priority of fulfilling the deceased's missed pillar.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding a Saroura man (not having had performed Hajj), who died and had not performed Hajj of Al-Islam, and for him was wealth’. Heasws said: ‘A Saroura would perform Hajj on his behalf, the one who does not have any wealth for him’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “

About the case of an al-Sarura (one who performs al-Hajj for the first time) who dies without performing Hajjahta al-Islam and has an asset, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘An al- Sarura (one who performs al-Hajj for the first time) who does not have any asset performs al-Hajj on his behalf.’”
